value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for user acceptance testing with a person's sign-off
value.lets_workers: Write personas and acceptance criteria before testing, have a person agree to the criteria, turn them into scenario scripts, run each script and record what was observed as it happened, propose a finding for every defect, compile the results by a fixed rule, and keep a person's go or no-go as a noun.

flow.when: When a surface, page or change needs acceptance testing.
Before any testing, from the personas and the change.
A person agrees to the exact criteria version; a person's verb.
Once per script and build, by an agent or a person.
When the planned sessions are in; deterministic.
A person records go, no_go or go_with_conditions; a person's verb.

guardrails: Criteria come first and are agreed by a person; a criterion changed after testing starts is a new version, and its runs are repeated.
Record what was observed, as it happened. Never edit a result to match the expected one.
Every failed or blocked step becomes a proposed finding with its evidence.
Only a person signs off. A recommendation from the results is advice, not the decision.
Made-up test data only. No real names, contact details or case details, ever.
complements: Accessibility findings go through the accessibility audit pack, which cites WCAG success criteria.
Each defect's fix, verification and guard go through the findings to fixes pack.
The launch readiness pack pins a sign-off as evidence before an owner decides on launch.

value.title: How acceptance testing runs from personas to a person's sign-off
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: draft-personas writes who the surface is for, as assumptions.
write-acceptance-criteria writes what must be true for each persona, before anyone tests.
agree-criteria: a person agrees to an exact criteria version.
write-scenario-scripts turns the agreed criteria into steps a person or a browser-driving agent can follow.
run-scenario follows one script on one build and records each step's result as it happens.
compile-results derives each criterion's verdict and a recommendation by fixed rules.
sign-off: a person records go, no_go or go_with_conditions, with reasons.
rules: Testing starts only from an agreed criteria version, pinned by digest.
A run on a different build or criteria version than its script ends blocked instead of guessing.
Observed results are recorded in plain words; expected results are never copied into them.
A failed, blocked or not-run step stays on the record; a rerun is a new session.
A no-go is a useful result, not a failure of the testing.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

roles.accountable_person: Agrees to the criteria and signs off. Usually the person who owns the outcome, such as a program manager.
roles.runner: An agent or a person who follows a script. A runner with assistive technology is a person unless an agent's tool truly is that technology.
roles.compiler: A deterministic worker that derives verdicts; it does not judge.

sources: Acceptance criteria in given, when and then form follow common behavior-driven practice; the wording here is original.

value.title: How to write a persona for acceptance testing
value.category_reason: A reusable method for writing personas; the personas themselves are seed hypotheses.
a_persona_holds: One primary goal, in the persona's words
The context they work in and any time pressure
Device, screen width, input modes and any assistive technology
How much they know about the domain
What success looks like to them
What they must never be asked to do, such as share a client's details
rules: Write goals and situations, not demographics or stereotypes.
Include at least one persona who uses only a keyboard or a screen reader, and one on a small screen, unless the brief says why not.
Personas are assumptions. Each says what evidence would confirm or contradict it, and later evidence can replace it.
Made-up only: a role label, never a real person's name, story, photo or contact details.
good_label_examples: Volunteer coordinator on a phone between shifts
Retired volunteer using a screen reader at home

value.title: How to write acceptance criteria that can be checked
value.category_reason: A reusable method for writing testable criteria.
value.form: Given a starting state, when the persona does one thing, then something a person or a deterministic check can observe happens.
rules: One behavior per criterion, with a then that names what is seen, not how it is built.
Priority is must, should or could. Every persona gets at least one must criterion.
Accessibility criteria cite their WCAG 2.2 success criteria from the accessibility audit checklist.
A time-on-task criterion states its threshold and how the time is measured, such as from the first page load to the moment the field is focused.
Content criteria say who must understand the wording, such as a volunteer with no technical background.
Error criteria say what the persona sees after a mistake and how they recover.

value.title: Made-up test data for acceptance testing
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule for which data a test may use.
use: Names that are role labels or plainly invented, such as Test Volunteer A.
Email addresses only at reserved example domains (example.com, example.org, example.net), and only on a test target.
Phone numbers only from reserved fictional ranges, and only on a test target.
never: Real people's names, stories, contact details, case notes or photos.
Anything pasted from a real inbox, case file or spreadsheet.
Credentials of any kind; a step that needs one is blocked until a person provides access outside the record.
value.on_live_targets: On a live public target, a step that would submit, pay or create an account is recorded as not_run unless a person named a test target for it.

value.title: How a failed step becomes a finding
value.category_reason: A zero-call mapping from an observed failure to a finding's kind, severity and evidence.

finding_kind.error: The surface does something other than its agreed criterion says, such as a button that does nothing.
finding_kind.design_flaw: It works as built, but the persona cannot finish, is misled or needs help to go on.
finding_kind.annoyance: The persona's own frustration, quoted exactly; record who said it and when.
finding_kind.issue: The environment or process got in the way, such as a missing test target or a build that changed mid-session.

provisional_severity.P0: The run exposed personal data or a credential; stop and route it to the security review pack.
provisional_severity.P1: A must criterion fails for a persona with no workaround they could find.
provisional_severity.P2: A must criterion needs a workaround, or a should criterion fails.
provisional_severity.P3: Cosmetic, or a could criterion fails.

evidence: The script and step number, the build and the criteria version
A screenshot digest and the region that shows the problem
The time and what was observed, in plain words
For an annoyance, the person's exact words

value.title: How criterion verdicts and the recommendation are derived
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic derivation: the same sessions always give the same verdicts.

criterion.met: Every step that checks it passed, in the latest included session for each persona it names.
criterion.not_met: At least one such step failed.
criterion.not_tested: No step failed, but at least one was blocked or not run, or a named persona has no included session.

value.included_sessions: Only sessions run on the agreed criteria version; others are listed as excluded with the reason.

recommendation.recommend_no_go: Any must criterion is not_met, or any P0 or P1 finding linked to the sessions is open.
recommendation.incomplete: No must criterion is not_met and nothing blocking is open, but at least one must criterion is not_tested.
recommendation.recommend_go: Every must criterion is met and no P0 or P1 finding is open.

value.rule: The recommendation is advice for the person who signs off; it never decides.

value.title: Record checks for sign-offs, with made-up golden sign-offs
value.category_reason: Deterministic checks with made-up known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes them.
value.purpose: Checks every sign-off must pass before anyone relies on its decision. The three made-up good sign-offs (a no-go, a conditional go and a clean go) pass all of them; each made-up bad sign-off fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: The decision is go, no_go or go_with_conditions.
The sign-off names the signer's role.
An agent never signs off, under any role name.
The sign-off is dated in UTC.
The signer says why, in their own words.
The decision names the exact results summary it read.
The decision names the exact agreed criteria.
A go with an unmet must criterion or an open P0 or P1 finding lists each accepted risk.
Every accepted risk says why and who owns it.
A conditional go lists its conditions.
Every condition has an owner and a date.
A no-go says what happens next.
A sign-off holds no email addresses or phone numbers.
